_doc: SemiAnalysis subset for the dc-delay-risk dashboard (tab 'SemiAnalysis'). Hand-built 2026-11-09 from the primary text and charts of four SemiAnalysis pieces; read by build_dc_delay.py (independent_views), which adds the registry comparison per state and the registry rows that cite SemiAnalysis.
SemiAnalysis is independent research (a continuous newsletter source), not a broker: no ratings, no price targets. GW content only (Felipe, 2026-11-06).

Basis: datacenter IT capacity. The 2026-09-15 piece states it ('+38GW of Datacenter IT capacity delivered in the US in 2027'); the 11-01 piece does not restate it. Never mix with facility, generation-nameplate or Aterio campus GW.

Tags per value: 'sa' = printed by SemiAnalysis (text, table or map); 'derived' = Capstone arithmetic on SemiAnalysis's printed values (formula in 'how'); 'range' = bounds implied by SemiAnalysis's table order and tiers. Most state values in the 11-01 charts are locked for non-subscribers.

exposure._note: Planned (not-started) 2028 capacity in states where a candidate backed a statewide pause, as of 2026-10-30 race ratings. SemiAnalysis: 'exposed to policy changes, not an estimate of delayed capacity'.
exposure.sweep_src: 1101 map: pause candidate wins every race
exposure.conditions_only_src: 1101 map: pause candidates lose every contested race; OH and OR have pause backers on both sides
exposure.candidates: Nine of the 20 nominees want a pause on new construction, 11 want conditions; split about even by party (1101).

pre_election_delay._note: Measured delay before the election (0915): capacity whose delivery date actually moves, project by project.

local.projects: An AWS campus in Ohio, a powered-land developer campus in Pennsylvania (NorthPoint, near Scranton), a site in Colorado
local.why_so_little: County moratoria stop at city lines; they freeze new applications rather than revoke approvals; short ones expire before 2028+ projects need the approval; other gates (litigation, equipment) already bind. ~80% of live restrictions contain no modelled planned capacity.

ny.instrument: EO 62 (2026-07-14): pause on discretionary DEC permits for new DCs >= 50 MW until a GEIS is done (up to Jul-2027); all affected capacity is 2028-or-later delivery.

tx.detail: ERCOT audit (Aug-3 directive): base-load projects face at most ~4 months of administrative delay; 17 facilities (6.6 GW) that cleared every other ERCOT gate are working through the audit to energize; Batch Zero backlog ~205 GW across 326 applicants; the Studied-Load study (was Sep-2 to Apr-9-2027) is paused and will miss Apr-9. Off-grid projects fall outside it. Written before the Sep-21 TCEQ freeze, which the 11-01 piece says closed the on-site-power escape route.

pre_election_delay.btm_note: Firm behind-the-meter equipment orders counted in the 0910 piece, more bound for Texas than any other state.

states.pause: Gina Hinojosa (D): until laws pass, est. to Sep-1-2027
states.note: 41.3% of the 13-state total. A prolonged TCEQ freeze is SemiAnalysis's biggest single risk to its forecast: a freeze through the 2027 session runs ~8 months from Sept, ~1 year if it waits for new rules, i.e. 5-9 months longer than a December restart.

states.pause: Keisha Lance Bottoms (D): no end given, ~6 months est.
states.note: OpenAI Project Camellia (Effingham County): 3.2 GW power commitment delivered 2028-2032; OpenAI pays Georgia Power's infrastructure, up to 1 GW curtailable, closed-loop cooling. Two PSC seats on the ballot.
Microsoft's largest state after Virginia. Three-year freeze on new sales-tax exemption applications since June; both candidates want the incentive gone and water paid for.

EO 2026-05 (GRID) conditions; HB 2650 passed the House 134-68.

state_ranges_note: Locked states (IN, MO, IL, WY, WV): bounds read from SemiAnalysis's 13-state table, which lists OK (2.1 GW adds) above PA (2.4 GW adds), so it is sorted by planned (unstarted) GW, and from the tiers (Tier 1 > 2 GW, Tier 2 1.5-2 GW, Tier 3 < 1.5 GW of unstarted 2028 capacity). Their sum is ~7.9 GW (40.5 planned - 32.6 printed or derived), inside the 6.6-9.5 GW the bounds allow.

items: Arizona is its largest state after Virginia (1101).
More than 5 GW of behind-the-meter nameplate signed in 2026 YTD, of which 2.7 GW with Chevron and well over 2 GW through turnkey leases with developers such as Crusoe (0910).
Project Kilby: Chevron's 2.67 GW off-grid plant serves a ~2 GW Microsoft campus in the Permian; fully islanded, so outside the ERCOT audit (0915).
Ohio becomes its largest state outside Virginia by 2028 (1101).
~44% of Pennsylvania's 2.4 GW of 2028 adds, including the Anthropic campus at Susquehanna (1101).
One of the three projects SemiAnalysis found delayed by a local moratorium is an AWS campus in Ohio (0915).
Ohio becomes its largest state anywhere by 2028, leased plus self-built (1101).
Shackelford County, TX (Vantage Frontier): flagship off-grid 1.4 GW IT campus on 500+ 4.25 MW Jenbacher J624 engines (0910).
Project Camellia, GA: 3.2 GW power commitment 2028-2032 (1101).
Goodnight, TX (built by Crusoe): buildings rising while its major generation permit is pending at TCEQ (1101).
Closed ~4.5 GW of datacenter IT capacity across three sites between Aug and Oct 2025, the start of GW-scale leasing (1018).
~15 GW of third-party capacity leased in 2026, more than 35 GW by 2028; ~39 GW by 2028 including Google, against Nvidia's 1.5 GW (0911).
Slightly under $1tn of binding, non-cancellable leases signed in 2026 YTD; a GW-scale pre-lease is typically 15-20 years at $30-50bn TCV per GW (1018).

contradicts.t: Texas went the other way from SemiAnalysis's base path.
contradicts.d: On 10-30 race ratings SemiAnalysis had Abbott (conditions only) favoured and a restart around ERCOT's Dec-10 report as the base path. Hinojosa won (provisional), so its 'biggest single risk' is now the live case: approvals frozen through the Jan-12 to May-31 2027 session, est. to Sep-1-2027. Our bear scenario already runs Texas to Sep-1.

contradicts.t: Texas 2028: SemiAnalysis's forecast vs Bernstein's credible pipeline.
contradicts.d: SemiAnalysis forecasts 18.0 GW of Texas adds in 2028, 16.7 GW of it not started. Bernstein (11-06, Aterio data) has 18 GW of not-started Texas pipeline targeting 2028 but only ~5 GW credible. Same headline size, very different conviction; bases also differ (IT vs Aterio nameplate).

contradicts.t: SemiAnalysis's 2028 is far bigger than our registry and the reference deck.
contradicts.d: US 2028: 62.2 GW (SemiAnalysis, IT) vs 47.4 GW in the deck's Aterio base (basis unstated) and {REG2028} GW of dated 2028 phases in our registry. The registry has nothing dated 2028 in PA, IL or IA and little in OK, OH and GA: it misses most of the unstarted 2028 capacity SemiAnalysis models (coverage column in the table).

new.t: Post-election exposure, from SemiAnalysis's own map values.
new.d: Governors-elect who back a pause won in TX, OH, GA and OR: 16.7 + 4.8 + 3.2 + 0.9 = 25.6 GW of SemiAnalysis's planned 2028 capacity (Capstone arithmetic), 84% of its 30.3 GW sweep case and 4.5x its 5.7 GW conditions-only floor. Exposed, not delayed.

new.t: State tiers and candidate pause lengths.
new.d: Tier 1 (> 2 GW unstarted): TX, OH, GA, AZ (+IN, low sensitivity); Tier 2: PA, OK (+MO); Tier 3: IL, OR, IA (+WY, WV). Pause-length estimates: TX to Sep-1-2027, OH 6-12 months, GA ~6, OK ~10, PA 6-12, OR to Jul-1-2027, IA ~6.

1.525 GW of ~20 GW inside local restrictions (7.6%) plus 0.8 of 1.4 GW exposed to New York's EO 62. The five EO-62 projects were added to the registry on 2026-11-09 (raw/ne_semianalysis_r3.csv); NorthPoint Hazle was not, for lack of a public MW figure.
SemiAnalysis sees ~10 GW of datacenter capacity without chips by end-2028 (HBM and N3 logic bind), which would slow new leases and orders from late 2027.

consistent.d: SemiAnalysis's test (does the project still need the approval, and does the hold outlast its schedule buffer?) is the same split as our waterfall: protected, pause ends first, delayed.

Frontier 1.4 GW IT = 10 x 140 MW in the registry; Camellia 3.2 GW = 5 x 640 MW grid tranches from 2028-06; Kilby 2.67 GW of generation for a ~2 GW campus implies generation / load ~1.34, against the 1.5 we use to convert generator nameplate (we carry Kilby at ~1.8 GW IT-eq).
SemiAnalysis's 7.6% delayed share of in-boundary capacity is already the anchor of our 'delay-local' guardrail.

caveats: SemiAnalysis's state values are mostly paywalled; ranges for IN, MO, IL, WY and WV are read from table order and tiers, not printed.
The exposure scenarios count planned 2028 GW in a state, not delayed GW. SemiAnalysis says a December Texas restart would not justify cutting 2027-28; a longer hold needs a fresh project-level test.
Election results are provisional; candidate positions are SemiAnalysis's reading, taken at face value.

catalysts.what: ERCOT files its audit report (target, not a fixed deadline); PUCT review Dec-17. Does not by itself reopen permitting.
Texas regular legislative session: the window Hinojosa's 'pause until laws pass' depends on.
Hinojosa takes office in Texas (state_rules.json, FundaAI 11-04).
Oklahoma regular session (rules window; Munson's pause is off the table after Mazzei's win).
Original end of ERCOT's Batch Zero study for Studied Load; ERCOT says it will miss it, no new date filed.
Oregon's DEQ permit hold and state-land pause end; New York's EO 62 pause runs up to Jul-2027.
S. 5653 (Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act): permitting reform plus DCs paying their transmission costs. Mostly economics, not capacity.
